entries.content:
MiniMax H3 Image and MiniMax H3 Image Highspeed are now available on AI Gateway. Generate images from text or edit existing images with one API key and no separate MiniMax account.

Both models support custom dimensions and aspect ratios, including 2K and 4K outputs. Use a text prompt to create a product visual or illustration, then pass the image back with instructions to change colors, subjects, or composition. The Highspeed variant offers faster generation with the same generation and editing options.

Use 

minimax/minimax-h3-image
or 
minimax/minimax-h3-image-highspeed
as the model name: 
      
import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';import { generateImage } from 'ai';
const { image } = await generateImage({  model: 'minimax/minimax-h3-image',  prompt: 'A blue ceramic vase with wildflowers on a sunlit wooden table.',  size: '2048x2048',  maxRetries: 0,  providerOptions: { minimax: { outputFormat: 'png' } },});
await writeFile('image.png', image.uint8Array);

To edit the generated image, pass it back with an instruction:

      
const { image: editedImage } = await generateImage({  model: 'minimax/minimax-h3-image',  prompt: {    text: 'Change the vase to terracotta and keep the flowers and setting.',    images: [image.uint8Array],  },  size: '2048x2048',  maxRetries: 0,  providerOptions: { minimax: { outputFormat: 'png' } },});
await writeFile('edited-image.png', editedImage.uint8Array);

Both models also support the OpenAI-compatible 

/v1/images/generations
and 
/v1/images/edits
routes. See the image generation guide for details.

Try MiniMax H3 Image in the model playground.

entries.title: Gemini 4 Carbon now available on AI Gateway
entries.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon from Google is now available on AI Gateway. It is available at 50% off through November 30, 2026:Gemini 4 Carbon is built for complex software engineering, sustained agentic work, and cybersecurity defense. entries.content:
Gemini 4 Carbon from Google is now available on AI Gateway. It is available at 50% off through November 30, 2026:

Gemini 4 Carbon is built for complex software engineering, sustained agentic work, and cybersecurity defense. It has a 1M-token context window for working with large codebases and long inputs.

On engineering tasks, Carbon carries demanding work through multiple stages, with improvements in coding, full-stack web development, and scientific reasoning. Its cybersecurity capabilities span finding vulnerabilities, validating their risk, and developing patches. Google also reports more reliable execution of multi-step plans, fewer unsupported claims, and better collaboration when requirements are ambiguous, helping agents follow through while respecting project constraints.

Use 

google/gemini-4-carbon
as the model name: 
      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'google/gemini-4-carbon',  prompt: 'Write a TypeScript helper that safely parses JSON and returns a fallback.',});
for await (const text of result.textStream) {  process.stdout.write(text);}

To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup:

      
npx vercel ai-gateway setup

Then select 

google/gemini-4-carbon
in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details.

Try Gemini 4 Carbon in the model playground.

entries.summary: Speed Insights and Web Analytics now fully support custom environments.Previously, data captured on deployments to a custom environment was attributed to the Preview environment. That data is now attributed to the custom environment it came from, so you can track performance and traffic for staging, QA, or canary environments separately from Production and Preview.You can view this data in several
entries.content:
Speed Insights and Web Analytics now fully support custom environments.

Previously, data captured on deployments to a custom environment was attributed to the Preview environment. That data is now attributed to the custom environment it came from, so you can track performance and traffic for staging, QA, or canary environments separately from Production and Preview.

You can view this data in several places:

  • Dashboard: use the Environment dropdown in Speed Insights and Web Analytics to pick a custom environment

  • CLI: query it with the 

    vc metrics
    command

  • Query builder: filter and break down by environment

  • Aggregation API: query it programmatically (Web Analytics only)

This change only affects how data is attributed. No new data points are collected, and no configuration changes are needed.

Custom environments are available on Pro and Enterprise plans. Learn more in the environments documentation.

entries.content:
Vercel Sandbox now creates snapshots up to 10x faster. Median time to snapshot is under 0.4 seconds, down from 4.4 seconds. Snapshot restore speed has also improved by 50% from 500ms to 250ms at p50.

Snapshots are now able to write and restore by re-using frames within the Vercel Hive Snapshot (VHS) format. VHS now indexes data in a more efficient way which means that more read and write operations can be done in parallel. Snapshots can now restore more of your Sandbox base image in parallel with user data, leading to overall faster operations.

Persistent sandboxes, the default, snapshot automatically when a session stops and resume from the latest snapshot. This applies to all new snapshots, with nothing to configure. Existing snapshots keep the previous format.

Learn more in the snapshots documentation.

entries.content:
AI Gateway Production Index — November 2026

Every month, AI Gateway routes more than 100 trillion tokens between production applications and AI labs. That traffic gives us a view of what AI usage looks like in today’s enterprise and startup landscape across language, decision, voice, image, and video models. We publish it here monthly. See the Production Index reports from August, September, and October.

Copy link to headingNovember 2026 Summary

  • In six weeks, decision models grew to one in four gateway requests, while accounting for half a cent of every dollar spent. Close to a third of all paid teams used one in October. Among teams processing over 10 billion tokens a month, seven in ten used a decision model.

  • About 11% of paid teams used a voice model in October, up from 4% in July.

  • OpenAI and Anthropic now reach about the same share of paid teams, and new teams in October picked Anthropic nearly two to one. OpenAI’s share of gateway spend, meanwhile, is up by two-thirds since December.

  • More than half of language-model requests went to models less than two months old, up from less than three in ten. Within one month of a typical model’s peak usage, three in four of the teams using it have moved on.

Copy link to headingDecision models account for 26% of all requests

Production AI is splitting into two jobs: generation and judgment. Until recently, when software needed to make a quick call, a team could use either a fixed rule that was cheap but rigid, or a language model that was smart but slow and expensive.

Decision models are now a third option. They classify, score, or pick between choices instead of generating text, and cost about a seventieth as much per request as a language model.

They arrived on AI Gateway in mid-September, and there are now 15 decision models available from eight different vendors. In October, nearly a third of paid teams on AI Gateway used a decision model. About 11% of paid teams used a decision model without sending a single request to a text-generating model.

Decision models cost far less per token and give very short answers, so even though they received about one in four gateway requests in October, they accounted for just 0.53% of total spend.

Almost all of that request volume went to Jev from TypeSafe AI, which alone received nearly four times Anthropic’s total requests. For every $1 teams spent on Jev, they spent $64 on Anthropic models.

Decision models are most common among the teams that run the most AI. Just over one in five teams running fewer than 10 million tokens used a decision model in October. At 100 million to 1 billion tokens, nearly half used one. Above 10 billion, seven in ten did.

This is partly because big teams use more of everything. The top 1% of teams by spend use a median of 29 different models, and the bottom tenth use only one. It’s also volume. The more requests a team sends, the more it has to gain from a model that makes simple decisions faster and far more cost-effectively.

Copy link to headingVoice adoption is up 2.6x since July

About one in nine paid teams used a voice model in October, up from one in 24 in July, an increase of 161%.

New teams are using voice, and existing teams are adding it. Among teams that paid in both July and October, the share using voice went from 5% to 14%.

Teams that use voice are also using more of it. The share of teams sending at least 100 voice requests a month grew fivefold, and six in ten of September’s voice teams returned in October, up from fewer than half in July.

A spoken conversation with an AI app takes three steps:

  • A voice model turns the user’s speech into text

  • A language model writes the reply

  • Another voice model reads the reply back to the user

Most voice teams use just one or two of these pieces. Use of speech-to-text models has nearly tripled since July, and text-to-speech has more than tripled.

Some models do all three steps on their own. In July, about a quarter of voice teams used one of these all-in-one models, and one in six assembled the pieces themselves. By October, those numbers had swapped.

For most teams, voice is a new way for users to talk to an app or agent they already have. Teams’ preferred language models stay in the middle, and they can add voice at one end or both.

Copy link to headingAnthropic wins new teams two to one, and OpenAI’s share of spend is up two-thirds

Last December, 70 of every 100 paid teams on AI Gateway used an OpenAI model and 48 used an Anthropic model. By October, the two labs were nearly level, with OpenAI at 55 and Anthropic at 54.

Both labs now reach more of the teams that have been on the gateway since December, but Anthropic’s reach grew more. The share of these teams using Anthropic rose from about half to two-thirds, while OpenAI’s rose from about three in four to four in five.

Most of Anthropic’s gain came from new teams. In October, it was the first-choice lab for nearly twice as many of them as OpenAI.

But among the biggest teams, both labs already have nearly everyone. More than nine in ten of the top 1% by spend use both Anthropic and OpenAI. With these teams, the labs now compete for how much of the work each one gets.

On that measure, Anthropic still leads, but OpenAI has gained ground. OpenAI now takes nearly 15 cents of every dollar spent on the gateway, up from about 9 in December, while Anthropic’s halved to about 32 cents over the same period.

Copy link to headingMost AI traffic now runs on models less than two months old

Teams are moving to new models almost as fast as labs release them. More than half of October’s language-model requests went to models less than 60 days old. Before September, that share had never passed three in ten.

Within each model family, a new version arrives every 61 days at the median, and a typical model peaks within a month of launch. Four weeks later, three in four of the teams using it at its peak aren’t using it anymore, whether or not a successor has shipped in the family. Most of those teams are still on AI Gateway, using other models.

Teams switch models frequently, usually to something newer, and often to another lab. In October, about half of teams running at least 10 million tokens a month changed their most-used model. Four in five of those moved to a more recent release, and six in ten moved to a different lab.

Older models stay in use, often alongside a newer primary model. Seven in ten teams running at least 10 million tokens a month still used a model at least ten months old in October, but for the typical team it ran less than 3% of its tokens.

AI models now have a half-life of about six weeks. That means that, to the teams using them, labs are only as good as their latest model and have to re-earn their business with every new one.

Copy link to headingAlso in October’s data

  • Opus 5.5 was the top model by spend in its first full month. It took about one in seven dollars across all teams. Four of the six most widely used models on AI Gateway are Anthropic’s: Sonnet 5.5 (reaching 26% of paid teams), Haiku 5.5 (22%), Haiku 4.5 (20%), and Opus 5.5 (18%). Jev (28%) and GPT-6 Luna (19%) are the other two.

  • Image and video both had their biggest month yet on AI Gateway. More teams than ever are putting spend on them, and the largest teams are adopting them the fastest. About a third of the top 1% of teams by spend now use an image model, up from a quarter in July. One in six use a video model, up from one in ten.

  • OpenAI’s newest image model, GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst, took the lead in image spend in its first full month, followed by its Flare and GPT-Image-2 models. ByteDance’s Seedance 2.5 led video spend for a third month running, ahead of Google’s Veo 3.1 and Kuaishou’s Kling 3.0.

Copy link to headingAbout this data

This report uses anonymized, aggregate traffic routed through Vercel AI Gateway through October 2026.

A few notes on measurement:

  • Spend is estimated at published list prices; actual bills may differ.

  • Paid teams are teams with at least one paid request in the month. Team size is measured by a team’s total tokens that month.

  • Decision models are the models classified as decision models in the AI Gateway model list.

  • Each model version is counted separately. A model’s age is measured from that version’s first day on AI Gateway, and gateway history begins October 20, 2025.

  • Switching rates compare paid teams with at least 10 million tokens in both September and October. A team’s most-used model is measured by tokens.

  • Voice figures begin June 22, 2026. Teams that “assembled the pieces” used speech-to-text, a language model, and text-to-speech on the same day.

  • A new team’s first-choice lab is the lab it sent the most language-model requests to in its first month.

  • All figures use the most recent data and protocol available; prior months may be revised as methodology is updated.

Read more about our methodology, and explore or download the public data.

entries.content:
The Workflow SDK now sends event writes and stream writes to Vercel Workflows over a WebSocket by default, replacing one HTTP request per write, or per write group for streams. No code change is needed beyond upgrading to 

workflow@5.2.0
or later.

Once you deploy the upgrade, new runs use it. In-flight runs finish on the deployment they started on.

      
npm install workflow@latest

Existing streaming code works as is. A step that writes a burst of chunks, like AI tokens, sends them over the WebSocket once it opens:

      
import { getWritable } from "workflow";
async function streamChunks(chunks: string[]) {  "use step";  const writer = getWritable().getWriter();  for (const chunk of chunks) {    await writer.write(chunk);  }  writer.releaseLock();}
export async function streamingWorkflow(chunks: string[]) {  "use workflow";  await streamChunks(chunks);}

Copy link to headingStreams keep pace with AI output

In a benchmark replaying an AI agent's token stream, v5.2.0, which writes streams over a WebSocket by default, delivered the full response 4.2× faster than v4.8.12, with no chunk delayed over a second.

Copy link to headingFewer HTTP requests for event writes

Every step start and completion is an event write, now sent over the WebSocket, so workflows with many steps make fewer HTTP requests. The added efficiency also improves performance and reduces costs. The queue handler opens the connection for every delivery.

Copy link to headingGet started

Read the Vercel World documentation to get started. If you're on 4.x, start with the upgrade guide, since v5 is a major release.

entries.content:
Disk space for Vercel builds has increased from 32 GB to 64 GB on Basic and Standard machines, matching the capacity already available on Enhanced and Turbo.

The additional space provides more room for the packages your project uses and the files generated during a build, reducing the risk of running out of disk space.

The change applies automatically across all plans and build machine types at no additional charge, with no configuration changes required.

Learn more in the build machine documentation.

entries.content:
Vercel Container Registry now supports compressed image layers of up to 2 GB each, up from 500 MB, the total image size limit stays 15 GB.

The registry works with standard workflows like 

docker push
, 
docker pull
, and 
docker tag
, and pushing an image creates the repository on the fly. 
      
docker buildx build --push -t vcr.vercel.com/team/project/repository:tag .

Repositories can be made public for read-only pull access by any Vercel team, or shared with specific teams up to 100 from the dashboard or with 

vercel vcr permissions
. The Vercel Managed Images that Vercel Sandbox runs on are served from ordinary public repositories, built with the same public-repository feature any team can use for its own images.

Manage repositories, images, and tags with the 

vercel vcr
CLI commands in Vercel CLI v58.3.0 or later, and log CI workflows in from GitHub Actions with the 
vercel/vcr-action/login
action using GitHub OIDC, which removes the need for long-lived registry credentials. If background optimization of a pushed image fails, the image shows an error status in the dashboard, and pushing the same image again retries the conversion.

See the documentation for the full setup.

entries.content:
Claude Fable 5.2 from Anthropic is now available on AI Gateway.

Fable 5.2 is built for open-ended technical work and improves on earlier Fable models in coding, reasoning, and vision. It can run long, ambiguous tasks unattended, and works as an orchestrator that hands simpler tasks to smaller models, or as an advisor that other Claude models consult on harder problems. It also communicates more clearly and generates output faster than earlier Fable models. Effort runs from 

low
to 
max
, with 
high
as the API default.

Fable 5.2 has cybersecurity and biology safety classifiers enabled. Access to Claude Fable 5.2 requires data retention. Anthropic does not support Zero Data Retention for the model. Prompts and completions are retained for 30 days and are not used to train Claude. If your team has ZDR turned on, AI Gateway returns an error instead of sending the request to Fable 5.2.

To keep requests served when a classifier is triggered, use model fallbacks. Add a 

models
array to 
providerOptions.gateway
, and AI Gateway tries each model in order when the cybersecurity classifier declines a request.

Call it through the AI SDK, the Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages APIs, or a coding agent connected to AI Gateway. Use 

anthropic/claude-fable-5.2
as the model name: 
      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'anthropic/claude-fable-5.2',  reasoning: 'high',  prompt: 'Review this login handler for security bugs.',  providerOptions: {    gateway: {      models: ['anthropic/claude-opus-5.5', 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5'],    },  },});

This request falls back to Opus 5.5, then Sonnet 5.5, if the cybersecurity classifier declines it. The 

models
option works the same way on every AI Gateway API format.

To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup:

      
npx vercel ai-gateway setup

Try Claude Fable 5.2 in the model playground.
